title: eieio service
description: A graph of block instances on one node (SERVICE-SPEC). The file on disk is TOML; this describes the equivalent structure, which is what DAEMON-SPEC §2 promises regardless of the encoding. SERVICE-SPEC is the normative document and this is a structural gate derived from it: the rules it cannot express are listed in `x-not-enforced-here`.

name.description: The service's name, unique per node. A path component in the management API and a filename on disk, which is why it is held to the same pattern as everything else that is both.

autostart.description: Whether the daemon starts this service at boot (DAEMON-SPEC §3). Absent means false.

blocks.description: Block instances, keyed by id. The key IS the identity (SERVICE-SPEC §2): `name` is a label, and connections, layout annotations and API paths all address the id.

connections.description: The wiring, one string per edge: `<id>.<port> -> <id>.<port>`. Ids only — the moment a connection may name a block, a name is load-bearing again.

ui.description: The Designer's annotations: canvas positions, viewport, notes (DESIGNER-SPEC §4). The daemon MUST parse this and MUST NOT interpret it, so it has no schema here and never will.

name.description: A label for people and agents. Optional, repeatable, and meaningless to a host — nothing resolves by it.

block.description: The block reference the block manager resolves, pulls and digest-verifies (SCOPE §3.6, DAEMON-SPEC §4). Its grammar is the registry's, not this format's.

props.description: Property expressions by name (ABI-SPEC §11). Every value is a string because every property is an expression and a literal is a trivial one; a number here would invent the second kind of property ABI §11 exists to refuse.

connection.description: `<id>.<port> -> <id>.<port>`. Whitespace is permitted around the arrow and nowhere else.

x-not-enforced-here: A connection naming an instance the file does not define (SERVICE-SPEC §7): JSON Schema cannot compare a string's contents against sibling object keys.
The same edge twice: `uniqueItems` would catch two identical strings but not `a.out->b.in` beside `a.out -> b.in`, which are the same edge.
`err` as a destination (ABI-SPEC §6.4): the pattern admits any port name on either side, because it is the direction that makes it wrong.
Whether a property expression parses and passes static analysis (EXPR-SPEC §10).
Whether a connection's ports exist on the referenced blocks' manifests, which needs the blocks resolved (SERVICE-SPEC §7 stage 2).
